properties.statement: `open_questions` RETURNING `count: 0` READS AS AN ALL-CLEAR AND IS NOT ONE — AND THE PROOF IS THAT A DOWNSTREAM DOC HAD TO GROW A HAND-WRITTEN WARNING. Reported by api-boss `5d608b85` (dev_storyflow, 2026-08-07), and previously by api-boss `07426210` on 2026-08-03, so it has now bitten twice. open_questions answers a narrow and correct question: what did we already PUT TO THE USER that is still waiting. In the SAME session that read `count: 0`, loop_status owed 69 gaps never asked, 26 structural defects, 20 capabilities claiming built with no check, and 20 built-but-never-checked. BOTH NUMBERS ARE CORRECT. They are answers to different questions, and nothing in either output says so. EVIDENCE IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the fleet's own boss cold-start card had to grow the line '⚠ count: 0 is NOT an all-clear' because arriving seats were reading it as one — and the reporter's own framing is the sharp part: a caveat maintained in a downstream document is a defect that was routed around rather than fixed. FIX SHAPE: when count == 0, have open_questions say what it does NOT cover and point at loop_status. One clause in the payload retires the caveat everywhere it was copied to. THE REPORTER GROUPED THIS with two others from the same day as one actionable class — three cases where a reflow2 surface returned a REAL, CORRECT number that answered a different question than the reader's: merge scores that silently feed deletions, open_questions vs the loop's debt, and per-session vs fleet-wide totals. In all three the fix is the same shape: LET THE OUTPUT STATE ITS OWN SCOPE.
